text:
incident-bot: [SEV2] Alerts: runtime-serving us-west-2 - multiple pods OOM and restarting. Symptoms: CUDA OOM, container exits, node kubelet flapping. Suspected: kvcache/paged-attn allocator fragmentation -> slow memory creep. Auto-mitigation: none, rate increase detected.

alice_oncall: seeing the same, dashboards spike at 03:12 UTC. Errors in pod logs show repeated 'cudaErrorMemoryAllocation' and 'allocator: unable to commit page'.

raj_runtime: hit this pattern before - KV page fragmentation slowly eats resident until OOM. Likely long-lived chat sessions + large seq lenses.

marta_sre: any customer-facing errors? ops shows 502s to hosted-api route /v1/generate, about ~8% error rate in last 10m. Not huge but trending.

chris_runtime: adding initial triage notes:
- grep pod logs: `kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-svc-5f9d | tail -n 200` -> repeated: `allocator.cpp:734 evict failed, free_pages=12, request=128`
- dmesg has cuda OOM bump messages on nodes gpu-04/gpu-07
- node events: kubelet eviction pressure, pod restartCount incrementing

alice_oncall: ok. plan: (1) reduce incoming rate to impacted pool, (2) patch allocator env to be more aggressive on compaction, (3) route critical customers to fallback region/model. Anyone can flip the routing?

marta_sre: I can scope traffic. Suggest scaling down max_concurrency on pool to 1 and disable long-lived converse sessions for now. Will post exact command.

runbook-bot: runbook 'kvcache-fragmentation' found -> recommended mitigations: trigger kv-compact, reduce batch_size, restart pods with `KV_COMPACT=true` env, increase eviction aggressiveness `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.6`.

raj_runtime: prefer avoiding full cluster restart. Steps I'd take now:
1) Apply patch to deployment: set env `KV_COMPACT=true` and `KV_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.55`
2) Roll pods one-at-a-time (canary first) with `kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime-svc -n runtime --selector=region=us-west-2 --timeout=5m`
3) If OOM persists, set `PAGED_ATTENTION=disabled` in runtime config and roll canary.

chris_runtime: note: disabling paged-attention will increase latency/cost but prevents allocator fragmentation. Good short-term mitigation. Also lower `MAX_SEQ_LEN` via config or per-route to 1024.

alice_oncall: marta, please throttle ingress to region and add rate-limiter rule for heavy sessions. Raj/chris, start the canary with KV_COMPACT first. I'll notify support.

marta_sre: throttling ingress: `kubectl patch cm igw-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"us-west-2-rate":"800r/s"}}'` -> applying now.

marta_sre: ingress patched, saw 30% drop in attempts to impacted pool. Monitoring latency and error rate.

raj_runtime: starting canary patch to one pod set with `KV_COMPACT=true`. Watch logs.

raj_runtime: canary logs show compaction running, memory stabilized on canary after ~90s. No immediate OOM.

chris_runtime: good signal. start rolling rest with 1 pod at a time. Keep `PAGED_ATTENTION` untouched for now.

alice_oncall: rolling restart in progress. ETA ~10m. Customer ops notified: non-critical degradation, some rate limits for a subset.

marta_sre: note: node gpu-07 still flapping, cordoned for maintenance: `kubectl cordon gpu-07` and draining non-critical pods.

raj_runtime: observation: historical metric `kv_page_frag_ratio` trending up for 48h - compaction didn't run frequently enough with our default threshold. Need follow-up to tune compaction cadence.

chris_runtime: after roll, error rate fell to ~1.2%. latency up ~15% on affected routes. Recommend follow-up ticket to:
- increase default compaction frequency
- add circuit to auto-disable paged-attn when frag ratio > 0.7
- add quick kill route to force kv-compact when memory drift detected

alice_oncall: Agreed. Creating post-incident action items. Also we should add a temporary dashboard alert: `kv_page_frag_ratio > 0.6` -> page SRE/team.

marta_sre: Customer Impact: Support reports 24 customers saw 4xx/5xx during window, highest impact between 03:08-03:25 UTC. We'll prepare a customer note if this persists.

runbook-bot: incident record created: INC-1761234567. Please add remediation steps taken.

alice_oncall: summary for handoff:
- Root cause: KV cache / paged-attn allocator fragmentation causing slow memory creep -> CUDA OOMs and node flaps.
- Short-term mitigation: ingress throttled, KV_COMPACT env enabled, rolling restart completed, cordoned problematic node, error rate reduced to ~1%.
- Next steps (post-mortem): tune compaction thresholds, add auto-disable for paged-attn at high frag, test compaction under load, add unit tests for allocator edgecases.

chris_runtime: leaving notes in PR #4821 for a follow-up patch to expose `KV_COMPACT` toggles and telemetry.

raj_runtime: marking my tasks: verify compaction metrics for 72h, run synthetic load to replicate, and prep hotfix if we see re-creep.

alice_oncall: thanks all — handing off to next oncall @marta_sre for watch. I'll post a short incident summary in #incidents later. :white_check_mark:

marta_sre: taking watch. will escalate if error >3% or any node flaps.

chris_runtime: +1. If anything spikes I'll flip `PAGED_ATTENTION=disabled` for the pool as emergency fallback.

incident-bot: Update: incident downgraded to MONITORING at 04:02 UTC.

alice_oncall: closing thread for now.
